en: In the *Śrī Dattātreyastuti*: I praise Dattātreya, the eternal Brahman, the stainless, the primordial deity, formless, manifest, and devoid of the qualities (*guṇa*). (1)

All is pervaded by consciousness; it is the sky of consciousness, clothed only by the directions, free from conceptual construction, devoid of appearance, and beyond both the seen and the seeing. || 2 ||

He is beyond the sphere of sensory experience, without support, the celibate practitioner, the lord of ascetics, the leader of the world of Brahmā, the perfect one, and the protector of the Supreme Self. || 3 ||
Released from the bondage of the snares of desire, endowed with that which is free from both purity and impurity;
knowing the equality of flavors in an empty dwelling, ever-knowing the pure and the utterly purified.
I salute Dattātreya, the supreme lord, the bestower of happiness, the ocean of supreme bliss, whose ornament is the fame of his consciousness; may he who reaches the one who remembers him protect me.
I bow to Harṣavardhana, the bestower of the bliss of liberation;
I bow to him who is worshipped by all the scriptures—may he, who dwells within the minds of those who remember him, protect me.
I bow to that which destroys the wandering of saṃsāra, crushes the suffering of conceptual thought, and wards off the threefold affliction; may He, who comes to those who remember Him, protect me.
I bow to that which shatters the ocean of doubt, pierces through the three defects, and whose nature is the light of Brahman; may it reach the one who remembers it and protect me. 8.
I bow to the one who most dearly fulfills the desires of Bhārgava, who destroys distance, and who protects the integrity of the world; may he, who comes to those who remember him, protect me.
Salutations to you, the pacifier of the fire of time; salutations be to you, the beloved of the practitioners of yoga. Salutations to you, the son of Atri; salutations be to you, Dattātreya. || 10 ||
Salutations to you, the playful sustainer of the universe; let there be salutation to you, the Avadhūta.
Salutations to you, the delight of Anasūyā; let there be salutation to you, the one clad in the directions as his garment. || 11 ||
Salutations to you, the one to be realized by sentient beings, the witness of all beings; let there be salutation to you.
Salutations to you, the most secret, the play of consciousness; let there be salutation to you.

Salutations to you, the support of the field; let there be salutation to you, the emptiness of the field. Salutations to you, the cause of form; let there be salutation to you, whose shape is like the sky. || 13 ||
O Śrī Dattātreya, protect me; be gracious, O sky-clad one!
Forgive me, O Avadhūta; protect, protect me, O Śrī Guru! 14.
